A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same character-level perturbation study. All 19 pages of v3 and 21 pages of v4, including Appendices A–G, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection resolve the figures and tables; reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original GSM8K evaluations, perturbation ablations, tokenization experiments, response analyses and attention visualization in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds SQuAD evaluation results and layerwise linear-probe results in Figure 10.

M1.justification: The three perturbation methods, tokenization variants and prompting procedures are retained. The new linear probes diagnose representations of the existing model; they do not modify its architecture, training objective or perturbation-handling procedure.

E1.justification: v4 extends the GSM8K-centered evaluation to SQuAD reading comprehension and a constructed English target-word recognition dataset for probing. These introduce distinct task requirements. Although v3's limitations mention code generation, neither its main text nor appendices report a code-generation evaluation, so no removal of that coverage is established.

E2.justification: The evaluated model rosters, prompt-strategy alternatives and perturbation controls in corresponding retained experiments are unchanged. SQuAD uses the already studied Qwen3-30B(A3B) thinking and non-thinking modes. The newly cited work by Zheng et al. is discussed but not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: v4 adds two substantive evaluation protocols: EM/F1 evaluation on 1,500 uniformly sampled SQuAD validation instances, and layerwise probing with an 80/20 training/test split. The probes train exclusively on clean examples and evaluate held-out clean and perturbed inputs. Existing GSM8K settings are retained; the PDFs do not establish reruns of those experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5.2.3 and new Appendix B.6 add a direct representation-level diagnostic of the implicit-denoising hypothesis. Figure 10 compares clean-trained probes across layers under clean input, character-level tokenization, 50-Typo, 100-Shuffle and UCC-1. This substantially extends the mechanistic evidence beyond the retained attention and feature-similarity analyses, although only the 'river' case is displayed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new SQuAD table and probing figure continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds SQuAD EM/F1 results and layerwise probe accuracy curves. For example, newly reported non-thinking SQuAD EM/F1 is 63.2/81.48 for clean input and 7.67/9.23 under 1-Inj. The retained GSM8K prefix2 clean accuracy changes from 0.035 in v3 Table 2 to 0.935 in v4 Table 3. SQuAD shuffle-row labels conflict with the stated degradation trend, leaving their intended strength-to-score mapping unresolved.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations are added or revised. Existing perturbation definitions and mathematical calculations are retained; the new probing procedure is an empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: resilience to severe character-level corruption and abnormal tokenization, explicit high-level rewriting, and implicit low-level denoising. The additional experiments support existing claims without redefining their stated scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.3 replaces the RoPE-based explanation of shuffle robustness with preserved character content and tolerance of abnormal tokenization, and interprets the new probes as supporting implicit denoising. Section 8 updates the stated task scope to mathematics and comprehension. However, the conclusion still retains the RoPE speculation.

D1.justification: v4 supplies limited construction and training details for the new probes: approximately 20-word sentences, target versus related negative words, layer-specific hidden-state inputs and clean-only fitting. Probe dataset size and optimization details are unspecified. Existing prompts, substitution mappings, model-access links and generation hyperparameters in the appendices remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the SQuAD citation and a related-work paragraph on Zheng et al.'s findings about non-canonical tokenization, while removing the Su et al. RoFormer reference. Other reference changes principally update publication metadata for already cited works. The overall research positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: There are localized grammar and wording edits, expanded explanation in Section 5.2.3, added appendix cross-references and subsection B.6, and new impact and acknowledgements sections. Contact and publication-footer text also change. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds SQuAD Table 2 and probing Figure 10, and merges v3 Tables 3 and 4 into v4 Table 4 without changing their results. Existing displays shift with text reflow, but their visual design is largely retained. The new SQuAD caption says non-thinking mode despite footnotes identifying both modes.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful evidence beyond GSM8K, directly probes a previously hypothesized denoising mechanism, corrects the prefix2 control value and acknowledges closely related tokenization research. These yield a modest net improvement. The gains are limited by inconsistent SQuAD shuffle labels and mode caption, incomplete reproducibility information for the single displayed probing case, and RoPE speculation retained in the conclusion after its main-text explanation was replaced.
